evidence: src/infrastructure/OrderController.ts: updateOrderState checks ['paid','packed','shipped','delivered'].includes(state) and listOrdersByState checks ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered'].includes(state). The two lists duplicate each other and the domain OrderState, then cast with `state as OrderState`.

src/infrastructure/OrderController.ts: the same catch block (`error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'` then res.status(400).json) is repeated in placeOrder, updateOrderState, cancelOrder and listOrdersByState.
src/infrastructure/ProductController.ts: the same catch/message block is repeated in getStock (404) and getAllStock (400), so error-to-status mapping has no single home.
The `Array.isArray(req.params.X) ? req.params.X[0] : req.params.X` unwrapping appears in OrderController.updateOrderState, OrderController.cancelOrder and ProductController.getStock.
src/infrastructure/Server.ts: the error middleware `(err, req, res)` is a third copy of the error-to-JSON mapping, with a different status (500).
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is broadly one concern: infrastructure adapters made of in-memory repositories, HTTP controllers and server wiring. The two repositories are consistent with each other and implement the domain interfaces. The problem is in the HTTP adapter code. OrderController hard-codes the set of valid order states twice, as two separate string-literal arrays. These duplicate the domain's OrderState definition, and the two lists differ from each other. If OrderState changes, both arrays must be edited by hand. The `state as OrderState` casts show the controller re-implementing domain validation instead of using one authoritative source. The same try/catch error-to-HTTP mapping and the same Array.isArray path-parameter unwrapping are copy-pasted across handlers in both controllers, with no shared helper. Each handler also picks its own failure status (400 versus 404) instead of using one mapping rule.

violations.message: The valid order-state set is hard-coded twice as string-literal arrays in updateOrderState and listOrdersByState. This duplicates the domain's OrderState invariant and the two copies differ. The result is cast with `as OrderState` instead of using a single validator or the domain's own definition. The try/catch error mapping and path-param unwrapping are also copy-pasted across every handler.

The error-to-response mapping (try/catch with `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'`) and the Array.isArray param unwrapping duplicate OrderController's logic, with no shared helper. The status codes differ between handlers (404 versus 400).
The error middleware repeats the error-to-JSON mapping a third time, with its own status rule. Server.ts also embeds product seed data in the composition code.
